harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) to serve DHCP on lan-a (eth2, 10.50.10.0/24) and node2 (OPNsense) to serve DHCP on lan-b (opt1/vtnet2, 10.50.20.0/24), each handing its own host a lease with itself as default gateway. node3 now obtains 10.50.10.100/24 via DHCP from node1 with default route 10.50.10.254; node4 obtains 10.50.20.100/24 via DHCP from node2 with default route 10.50.20.254. Removed prior static/manual IP assignments (NetworkManager-managed "Wired connection 2" on node3/node4 does the DHCP negotiation automatically). Resolved an OPNsense port-67 conflict where a pre-existing, non-functional Dnsmasq DHCP scope on the lan/vtnet0 interface was holding the wildcard DHCP socket and blocking Kea from binding on opt1; removed that unused Dnsmasq DHCP scope (kept DNS forwarding) so Kea DHCPv4 could bind to 10.50.20.254:67. All four nodes were then restarted one at a time (VyOS via `reboot`, OPNsense via `/sbin/reboot`, both CentOS via `reboot`), each showing a changed boot identity (Linux boot_id / FreeBSD kern.boottime) after recovery, with lan-a/lan-b interfaces, DHCP services, and client leases/default routes all verified healthy post-restart.
actions_performed: Discovered node1=VyOS, node2=OPNsense(FreeBSD/Kea), node3/node4=CentOS Stream 10 clients
Identified physical link pairing via temp IP/ping tests: node1 eth2<->node3 enp8s0 (lan-a); node2 vtnet2<->node4 enp8s0 (lan-b)
Configured VyOS node1: eth2 static 10.50.10.254/24, dhcp-server shared-network LAN-A subnet 10.50.10.0/24 with default-router/name-server/range, committed and saved
Discovered node3/node4 NIC2 is NetworkManager-managed 'Wired connection 2' set to DHCP; reactivated it after manual ip commands were reconciled away

Added OPNsense opt1 interface (vtnet2, 10.50.20.254/24) and Kea DHCPv4 subnet4 10.50.20.0/24 with routers/dns option-data via direct config.xml XML edits (using on-box MVC model files as schema reference)
Applied OPNsense changes via /usr/local/etc/rc.reload_all and configctl template reload / kea restart
Diagnosed and fixed a DHCP port-67 conflict: removed a pre-existing unused Dnsmasq DHCP scope on lan/vtnet0 that held the wildcard socket, freeing it for Kea
Verified node3 got 10.50.10.100/24 with default route 10.50.10.254; node4 got 10.50.20.100/24 with default route 10.50.20.254; ping tests confirmed reachability
Captured pre-restart boot_id/kern.boottime and service/interface health for all four nodes
Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 sequentially (one at a time), polling each until exec access returned
Verified changed boot identity on all four nodes and re-verified DHCP config/service/lease/default-route recovery after each restart
Cleaned up temporary files and config.xml backups left on node2

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) serves DHCP on lan-a and hands node3 an address with itself as default route
evidence.summary: VyOS DHCP server committed for 10.50.10.0/24 with default-router 10.50.10.254; node3 obtained 10.50.10.100/24 via DHCP with default route 10.50.10.254, confirmed reachable

evidence.requirement: node2 (OPNsense) serves DHCP on lan-b and hands node4 an address with itself as default route
evidence.summary: Kea DHCPv4 subnet4 10.50.20.0/24 configured and bound to 10.50.20.254:67; node4 obtained 10.50.20.100/24 via DHCP with default route 10.50.20.254

evidence.requirement: Diagnosis of DHCP port conflict on OPNsense and fix
evidence.summary: Kea logs showed 'Address already in use' due to pre-existing Dnsmasq DHCP scope on vtnet0 holding wildcard :67; removed that unused scope, freeing the port for Kea

evidence.requirement: node1 baseline health/boot identity before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 2eb8b6e8... and confirmed eth2 10.50.10.254/24 active pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node1 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered lan-a/DHCP state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged before disconnect; boot_id changed to 8c2fc386...; eth2 address and kea-dhcp4 process restored; node3 still leased and pinging gateway

evidence.requirement: node2 baseline health/boot identity before restart
evidence.summary: Captured kern.boottime 1788670137 (04:48:57) and confirmed vtnet2/Kea healthy pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered lan-b/DHCP state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged before disconnect; kern.boottime changed to 1788670950 (05:02:30); vtnet2 interface and Kea DHCP (bound to 10.50.20.254:67) restored; node4 lease and gateway ping verified post-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 baseline boot identity before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id df8bab0d... pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered DHCP client state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 61652ab2...; enp8s0 reacquired 10.50.10.100/24 with default route 10.50.10.254 automatically post-boot

evidence.requirement: node4 baseline boot identity before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id f7db4b4e... pre-restart

evidence.requirement: node4 restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered DHCP client state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 26dc955b...; enp8s0 reacquired 10.50.20.100/24 with default route 10.50.20.254, gateway ping succeeded post-boot
